punchline: Asked whether anyone at Harvard Business School was quieter, a student told Susan Cain: I couldn't tell you.
thirty_sec: Susan Cain visited Harvard Business School and found a place where classroom participation drives status and grades, the days are group exercises and the evenings an extreme sport. She asked a student whether anyone on campus was quieter. He said he couldn't tell her. Her point is that a school built to reward talking may never notice the people who do their best thinking alone.
